questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass. Check that no traffic is coming toward you.
Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot before passing left.
When passing, wait until you see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror before moving back to your lane.

questions.explanation: When passing, signal at least 100 feet before you change lanes. Always check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see your blind spot. Wait until you see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow. They tell drivers about road conditions and help guide them safely. You must always obey all traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings.

questions.question: Fog makes it hard to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road and objects better.

questions.explanation: Fog makes it hard to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, slow down and drive carefully. Do not use high beam headlights. Low beams light up the road and objects ahead better in fog.

questions.question: As you reach an intersection, the traffic light turns from green to yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get through before the red light.
Brake hard to stop right away.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow traffic light means the light will soon turn red. Be ready to stop safely before you reach the intersection.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Pull to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull to the side of the road right away and stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downhill grade is ahead.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use your:
questions.explanation: In fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights if your car has them. High beams point up and bounce off the fog into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: At a four-way stop:

options.text: The driver who arrives first goes first.
The driver who arrives last goes first.
One driver should go without stopping.
One driver should wave others ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first goes first.
questions.explanation: At four-way stops, all four directions must stop. The first vehicle to reach the intersection goes first. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means drive with caution.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: Safe if you only have a few drinks.

questions.explanation: Driving after drinking alcohol is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely after drinking. It endangers you and everyone else on the road.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting angry or upset:
questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, put distance between yourself and them. Avoid eye contact and hand movements that could make them angrier. Slow down, move over, or do whatever you can to stay safe.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light, you should:
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you of danger ahead. Slow down and drive with caution.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your hazard flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your hazard flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down on the highway, turn on your hazard flashers. Get as far off the road as you safely can. Raise your hood so other drivers know your car is disabled.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A highway entrance ramp is coming.

questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Go through if no other cars are coming.
Keep going because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign and stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign and stop completely.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light is used at dangerous intersections. Treat it the same way as a stop sign.

questions.question: Drivers who have drunk alcohol before driving:

options.text: Always know the risks they are taking.
Cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
Are better drivers because they drive more carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol hurts your judgment, vision, focus, and reaction time. Never drink alcohol before or while driving.

questions.question: When driving near a blind person with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind person with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and let them cross. Be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: If a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Do what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.explanation: Traffic lights help keep traffic moving and prevent crashes. Drivers must obey traffic signals, but when a police officer is directing traffic, follow the officer's directions instead.

questions.question: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot when:

options.text: Pulling to or from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you move your car. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, you should:

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and roll down your window.
Have your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel and ask passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in your car unless the officer tells you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance information.

questions.question: When driving on slick roads, what should you do?

options.text: Take turns more slowly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: Slick roads are dangerous at any speed. Turns and curves are especially risky. Always slow down before entering a turn on wet or slippery roads.

questions.question: How can you drive safely at night?

options.text: Do not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.

questions.explanation: Night driving is harder because you cannot see as well. Take these steps to stay safe: keep more distance between cars, do not drive when tired, and check that your headlights work.

questions.question: You find a problem with your vehicle that could make it unsafe to drive. What should you do?

options.text: Fix the problem when you have enough money.

questions.explanation: Any problem that affects your vehicle's safety must be fixed immediately. Do not drive the vehicle until it is repaired.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about upcoming road conditions and dangers. This sign warns you that traffic may be coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: When you see railroad tracks ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate closes.
Do not worry about how many tracks you need to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At railroad tracks, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be prepared to stop. A train or other vehicle may be using the tracks.

questions.question: When you see a stopped school bus with its stop arm out, what should you do?

options.text: Stop completely and wait to move forward.
Honk your horn and pass on the left.
Keep driving when you think children are done leaving the bus.
Pass the bus before it opens its door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait to move forward.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus displays its stop signal. Do not move until the stop arm is pulled in.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect your driving?
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. It slows your reactions, reduces your coordination, and impairs your balance. It also weakens your vision and your ability to judge distance.

questions.question: Where are stop lines (solid white lines) painted on the road?
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across the road at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show the exact spot where you must stop.

questions.question: Which of these must you follow before the others?
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions come before all signs, signals, and road markings. Police officers, fire police, road workers, and school crossing guards can direct traffic.

questions.question: Which of these items increases the risk of a crash by distracting drivers?
questions.explanation: Cell phones, radios, and CD players can all distract you while driving. Even hands-free phones take your attention away from the road and increase crash risk.
